title: Finite-type ambient geometry and a common geometric-fibre dimension bound
statement: Let $p:T\to Y$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] between schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $Y$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and finite topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then $T$ also has such a finite Noetherian affine cover and finite topological Krull dimension. There exists $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, the fibre $T\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum] has topological Krull dimension at most $e$. Empty schemes and fibres have dimension $-\infty$ and are allowed. If an integer $N$ is a unit in every local ring of $Y$, it is a unit in every local ring of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0A3V, lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension (ordinary-fibre bound); geometric-fibre and source-dimension refinement by the affine polynomial presentation, using Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Polynomial.lean, MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_of_isNoetherianRing. This is the extracted argument of item proof step 1, not a verbatim statement of 0A3V.

proof.text: Choose the given finite affine cover $Y=\bigcup_{a\in A}V_a$, $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$, with $R_a$ Noetherian. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], for each $a$ choose a finite affine cover $p^{-1}(V_a)=\bigcup_{b\in B_a}U_{ab}$ with $U_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}S_{ab}$ and $S_{ab}$ a finite type $R_a$-algebra. The combined family is finite and covers $T$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose generators $s_{ab,1},\ldots,s_{ab,n_{ab}}$ and a surjective evaluation map $R_a[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_{ab}}]\twoheadrightarrow S_{ab}$. Set $e=\max(\{0\}\cup\{n_{ab}:a\in A,b\in B_a\})$. All these choices, including $e$, are made before choosing a geometric point. Empty index sets cause no problem.

source.place: Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type, and the preceding recollection of finite type ring maps

proof.text: For each pair $(a,b)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to the Noetherian ring $R_a$ and its finite type algebra $S_{ab}$. Thus every $S_{ab}$ is Noetherian, and the finite cover of step 1 is the required finite Noetherian affine cover of $T$. This uses neither separatedness nor affineness of intersections of charts.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; compare Morphisms Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian

proof.text: Choose a nonnegative integer $D$ with $\dim Y\le D$, possible by the finite-dimension hypothesis and the empty-space convention. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring], $\dim R_a=\dim V_a\le D$. By [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension], the polynomial ring in step 1 has dimension $\dim R_a+n_{ab}\le D+e$. A strict chain of primes of $S_{ab}$ pulls back under its surjective evaluation map to a strict chain of primes of this polynomial ring: inverse images are prime, and strictness follows by taking a preimage of an element in each difference of consecutive primes. Hence the definition [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim S_{ab}\le D+e$. The spectrum comparison then gives $\dim U_{ab}\le D+e$. Zero coordinate rings have dimension $-\infty$ and satisfy the same inequalities.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] to the finite open cover $(U_{ab})$ of $T$ and the bound $D+e$ from step 3. Its quasi-sober and $T_0$ hypotheses hold because schemes are sober by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. More explicitly, generic-point existence is quasi-sobriety; uniqueness implies $T_0$, since two points with the same closure would be two generic points of that irreducible closed subset. Thus $\dim T\le D+e<\infty$. If $T$ is empty its dimension is $-\infty$, so the conclusion still holds.

source.place: Tag 0B7I, lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions, open-cover consequence; Schemes Tag 01IS, lemma-scheme-sober

proof.text: Fix any algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and any $h:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$. Its source has one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so choose $a$ with its image $y$ in $V_a$. Then $h$ factors through the open subscheme $V_a$: its topological map and sheaf map simply restrict, with the local maps unchanged. Write $F=T\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with base open $V_a$, source open $U_{ab}$ and the entire second factor $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. It identifies $W_b=U_{ab}\times_{V_a}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with the inverse image of $U_{ab}$ in $F$. These opens cover $F$: the image in $T$ of every point of $F$ lies over $y$ and hence belongs to some $U_{ab}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $W_b\cong\operatorname{Spec}(S_{ab}\otimes_{R_a}\Omega)$ with the structural maps given by the two tensor inclusions.

source.place: Tags 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product, and 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; affine cover formulation: lemma-affine-covering-fibre-product

proof.text: For each $b$, the algebra $S_{ab}\otimes_{R_a}\Omega$ is generated over $\Omega$ by $s_{ab,i}\otimes1$, with the scalar inclusion $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Indeed its underlying tensor module is generated by pure tensors, and if $s=P(s_{ab,1},\ldots,s_{ab,n_{ab}})$ then $s\otimes c=(1\otimes c)P_\Omega(s_{ab,1}\otimes1,\ldots,s_{ab,n_{ab}}\otimes1)$, where the coefficients of $P_\Omega$ are the images in $\Omega$ of those of $P$; the tensor balancing relation moves each coefficient to the second factor. Finite sums of such expressions give every tensor. The multiplication and scalar inclusions are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], on the tensor module of [def-weil-module-base-change]. Evaluation, as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], therefore gives a surjection $\Omega[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_{ab}}]\twoheadrightarrow S_{ab}\otimes_{R_a}\Omega$. This is a generator calculation, requiring no flatness of $R_a\to\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, tensor-ring universal property and the generator calculation for its ring

proof.text: A field is Noetherian and has ring dimension zero: an ideal containing a nonzero element contains its inverse multiple $1$, so its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, and its only prime is $(0)$. Thus [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] applied to $\Omega$ gives $\dim\Omega[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_{ab}}]=n_{ab}$. Pulling a strict chain of primes back along the surjection in step 6 preserves its length by exactly the inverse-image and element-lifting argument of step 3. Consequently [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim(S_{ab}\otimes_{R_a}\Omega)\le n_{ab}\le e$, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim W_b\le e$. A zero tensor ring has empty spectrum and dimension $-\infty$, which also satisfies this bound.

The fibre product $F$ is a scheme, so [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives the quasi-sober and $T_0$ hypotheses as in step 4. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] to the open cover $(W_b)$ from step 5 with the common bound $e$ from step 7. It gives $\dim F\le e$. Since $e$ was fixed in step 1 independently of $\Omega$ and $h$, this proves the required uniform bound for every geometric fibre. Empty $F$, empty members, and even an empty cover of an empty $F$ are included in the cited open-cover statement. No comparison between ordinary and geometric fibre dimensions has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0B7I, lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions; the affine-presentation refinement of Morphisms Tag 0A3V to arbitrary field-valued points

proof.text: Finally, for each $t\in T$ the scheme morphism induces a unital local ring homomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y,p(t)}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ by [def-pc-scheme] (a morphism of locally ringed spaces). If $Nv=1$ in $\mathcal O_{Y,p(t)}$, its image satisfies $N\varphi(v)=\varphi(Nv)=1$. Thus $N$ is invertible in every local ring of $T$. When $T$ is empty this assertion is vacuous.
